label: hip
title: Conjecture
head: environment

label: thm:main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:main}
	For every $k\ge 2$ there exists $\gamma = \gamma(k)>0$ such that 
	 
	\[
		\mathrm{ex}(n,s)=g_k(n,s)=\min_\ell g_\ell(n,s)
	\]
	 
	whenever 
	 
	\[	
		\frac{k}{3k-1}n \le  s \le \left(\frac{k}{3k-1}+\gamma\right)n\,.
	\]
	  
	For instance, this holds for $\gamma(k)=(600k^6)^{-1}$.
head: environment

label: thm:mindeg
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:mindeg}
	Let  $k\ge 2$ and $n\ge s \ge 1$. If $H$ denotes a triangle-free graph on~$n$
	vertices with $\alpha(H)\le s$ and 
	 
	\[
		\delta(H) > \frac{k+1}{3k+2}n\,,
	\]
	 
	then $e(H) \le g_k(n,s)$.
head: environment

label: fact:1641
title: Fact
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The double counting argument 
	 
	\[
		\sum_{i=1}^r |N(V_i)|
		=
		\sum_{i=1}^r \sum_{v_j\in N(v_i)} |V_j|
		=
		\sum_{j=1}^r |N(v_j)|\,|V_j|
		=
		k\sum _{j=1}^r |V_j|
		=
		kn
	\]
	 
	establishes part~\ref{it:1641a}. If $H$ is a proper blow-up, then~\eqref{eq:neighbours} 
	yields 
	 
	\[
		r\delta(H) \le \sum_{i=1}^r |N(V_i)| \le r\Delta(H)
	\]
	 
	and part~\ref{it:1641b} follows.
head: environment

label: l:kregular
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Notice that every balanced blow-up $H(p)$ of $H$ is a proper blow-up of $J$ as well. 
	By applying this observation to a sufficiently large integer $p$ we learn that we may 
	assume, without loss of generality, that $H$ is a proper blow-up of $F$. 
	Now Fact~\ref{fact:1641}\ref{it:1641b} reveals  
	 
	\[
		\delta(H)\le \frac{kn}{3k-1} \le \Delta(H)\,,
	\]
	     
	which together with~\eqref{eq:1710} implies
	 
	\[
		\frac{d+1}{3d+2} < \frac{k}{3k-1} < \frac{d-1}{3d-4}\,.
	\]
	 
	Taking reciprocals we obtain 
	 
	\[
		3-\frac{1}{d-1} < 3-\frac 1k < 3-\frac 1{d+1}\,,
	\]
	 
	i.e., $d-1<k<d+1$.
head: environment

label: edges
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
As usual, we write the vertex set of $F$ in the form $V(F)=\{v_1, \ldots, v_r\}$. 
	Setting $x_i=|V_i|$ for $i\in [r]$ we have 
	 
	\begin{align*}
		2e(H) 
		&= 
		\sum_{v\in V(H)}\deg_H(v)
		=                                 
		\sum_{i=1}^r|V_i|\cdot|N(V_i)| \\
		&= 
		\sum_{i=1}^r x\cdot|N(V_i)|+\sum_{i=1}^r(x_i-x)\cdot|N(V_i)| \\
		&\le 
		x\sum_{i=1}^r|N(V_i)|+\sum_{i=1}^r(x_i-x)s
		\overset{\eqref{eq:1734}}{=}
		xkn+s(n-xr)
		=
		ns-x(rs-kn)\,, 
	\end{align*}	
	which proves the desired upper bound on $e(H)$.
	
	Suppose from now on that this estimate holds with equality and that $rs\ne kn$. 
	This means that $(x_i-x)|N(V_i)|=(x_i-x)s$ holds for every $i\in [r]$,
	or in other words that $x_i>x$ implies $|N(V_i)|=s$. This proves the second bullet.
	Now, if the first bullet fails, we have $|N(V_i)|=s$ for every $i\in [r]$ 
	and~\eqref{eq:1734} yields the contradiction $rs=kn$.
head: environment

label: blowupedges
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{blowupedges}
	Suppose that $k\ge 2$ is a natural number, $F$ is a $k$-regular graph 
	on~$3k-1$ vertices and $H$
	is an $n$-vertex blow-up of $F$. If $|N(Z)|\le s$ and $|Z|\ge (k-1)n - (3k-4)s$
	hold for every vertex class $Z$ of $H$, then 
	 
	\[
		e(H)\le g_k(n,s)\,.
	\]
	 
	Moreover, if $e(H)=g_k(n,s)$, then 
	\begin{enumerate}[label=\upshape({\itshape \roman*\,})]
	\item\label{it:2140a} $kn/(3k-1) \le s \le (k-1)n/(3k-4)$;
	\item\label{it:2140b} $H$ contains a vertex class of size $(k-1)n - (3k-4)s$;
	\item\label{it:2140c} the neighbourhood of each vertex class of $H$ containing 
		more than $(k-1)n - (3k-4)s$ vertices has size $s$.
	\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
In order to prove the desired upper bound on $e(H)$ we remark that Lemma~\ref{edges} 
	applied to $r=3k-1$ and $x=(k-1)n-(3k-4)s$ yields  
	 
	\[
		e(H)
		\le 
		\tfrac12\bigl[ns-\bigl((k-1)n -(3k-4)s\bigr)\bigl((3k-1)s - kn\bigr)\bigr]
		=
		g_k(n,s)\,. 
	\]
	 
	Let us now study the case that equality holds in this estimate. If clause~\ref{it:2140a} 
	failed, then the trivial upper bound $e(H)\le ns/2$ would contradict $e(H)=g_k(n, s)$.
	
	The remaining two clauses follow from the moreover-part in Lemma~\ref{edges} provided
	that its assumption $(3k-1)s\ne kn$ holds. So it remains to deal with the 
	case $s=kn/(3k-1)$. Now $(k-1)n - (3k-4)s = n/(3k-1)$ is at the same time the average 
	size of the vertex classes of $H$ and a lower bound on the sizes of these vertex classes.
	In other words, $H$ is the balanced blow-up $F\bigl(n/(3k-1)\bigr)$ 
	and~\ref{it:2140b},~\ref{it:2140c} hold trivially.
head: environment

label: fact:A1
title: Fact
body_md:
\label{fact:A1} 
	Let $k\ge 2$ be an integer.
	\begin{enumerate}[label=\upshape({\itshape \roman*\,})]
		\item\label{it:1112a} We have $\Gamma_{k-1}\subseteq \Gamma_{k}$. 
			Conversely, if we remove a vertex from $\Gamma_{k}$, then the resulting 
			graph is a subgraph of a proper blow-up of $\Gamma_{k-1}$. Consequently, 
			every subgraph of~$\Gamma_k$ is a subgraph of a proper blow-up of $\Gamma_\ell$ 
			for some $\ell\le k$.
		\item\label{it:1112b} The chromatic number of $\Gamma_k$ is $3$. 
		\item\label{it:1112c} Every independent set in $\Gamma_k$ is contained 
			in the neighbourhood of some vertex of $\Gamma_k$. In particular, $\alpha(\Gamma_k)=k$.
	\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The first part of~\ref{it:1112a} follows from $\Gamma_{k-1}\cong \Gamma_k - \{v_0, v_k, v_{2k}\}$.
	Furthermore, the graph $\Gamma_k^-=\Gamma_k-\{v_{k}\}$ 
	satisfies $N(v_0, \Gamma_k^-)\subseteq N(v_1, \Gamma_k^-)$
	and $N(v_{2k}, \Gamma_k^-)\subseteq N(v_{2k-1}, \Gamma_k^-)$,
	which proves~$\Gamma_k^-$ to be a subgraph of the blow-up 
	of $\Gamma_k - \{v_0, v_k, v_{2k}\}$ obtained by doubling the vertices~$v_1$
	and~$v_{2k-1}$. This establishes the second part of~\ref{it:1112a} and the 
	last part follows inductively.  
	
	Proceeding with~\ref{it:1112b} we observe that, due to~\ref{it:1112a}, 
	$\Gamma_k$ contains a pentagon~$\Gamma_2$ as a subgraph, whence $\chi(\Gamma_k)\ge \chi(\Gamma_2)=3$. 
	To verify the reverse inequality, we partition $V(\Gamma_k)$ into the three independent sets 
	$\{v_0, v_1, \ldots, v_{k-1}\}$, $\{v_k, v_{k+1},\ldots, v_{2k-1}\}$, and 
	$\{v_{2k}, v_{2k+1}, \ldots, v_{3k-2}\}$.

	Finally, let $S\subseteq V(\Gamma_k)$ be a nonempty independent set we want to cover by 
	the neighbourhood of an appropriate vertex. By symmetry we may suppose that $v_k\in S$, 
	which due to~\eqref{eq:1200} entails $S\subseteq \{v_1, v_2, \ldots, v_{2k-1}\}$. 
	Let $i, j\in [2k-1]$ be the smallest and largest index with $v_i, v_j\in S$. 
	Now $S\subseteq \{v_i, \ldots, v_j\}$, a further application of~\eqref{eq:1200} 
	shows $j-i \le k-1$, and altogether we have $S\subseteq N(v_{j+k})$.
head: environment

label: Vi
title: Fact
body_md:
\label{Vi}
	For every $i\in{\mathds Z}_{3k-1}$ we have
	 
	\[
		(k-1)n - (3k-4)s \le |V_i|\le 3s-n\,.
	\]
head: environment

title: Proof
head: environment

label: ag0
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{ag0}
	Let $k$ be a natural number.
	If for $n\ge s\ge 1$ the graph $H$ is an $n$-vertex blow-up of the Andr\'asfai graph 
	$\Gamma_k$ satisfying $\alpha(H)\le s$, then 
	 
	\[
		\pushQED{\qed} 
		e(H)\le  g_k(n,s)\,.\qedhere
		\popQED
	\]
head: environment

label: def:exan
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:exan}
	Given natural numbers $k\ge 2$, $n$, and $s\in [kn/(3k-1), (k-1)n/(3k-4)]$
	the family $\mathscr{G}^n_k(s)$ consists of all graphs obtained from $\Gamma_k$ by blowing up 
	its vertices
	\begin{enumerate} 
		\item[$\bullet$] $v_0$ and $v_k$ by $(k-1)n-(3k-4)s$, 
		\item[$\bullet$] $v_{2k-1}$ by $a$, $v_{2k}$ by $b$, where 
				$a,b\in [(k-1)n-(3k-4)s, 3s-n]$ are two integers summing up 
				to $(k-2)n-(3k-7)s$,
		\item[$\bullet$] and all remaining vertices by $3s-n$. 
	\end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: lem:2130
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:2130}
	If $H$ denotes an $n$-vertex blow-up of $\Gamma_k$ satisfying 
	 
	\[
		\alpha(H)\le s
		\quad \text{ and } \quad
		e(H)= g_k(n,s)
	\]
	  
	for some $k\ge 2$, then $kn/(3k-1)\le s\le (k-1)n/(3k-4)$
	and $H$ is isomorphic to some graph in $\mathscr{G}^n_k(s)$.
head: environment

label: eq:1847
title: Proof
body_md:
As usual we denote the vertex classes of $H$ corresponding to the vertices of $\Gamma_k$
	by $V_0, \ldots, V_{3k-2}$. Recall that by Fact~\ref{Vi} 
	we have 
	 
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:1847}
		(k-1)n - (3k-4)s \le |V_i|\le 3s-n
		\quad \text{ for every } i\in{\mathds Z}_{3k-1}\,.
	\end{equation}
	In particular, $H$ has the properties enumerated in the moreover-part of
	Corollary~\ref{blowupedges} and clause~\ref{it:2140a} corresponds to the estimates on $s$ 
	stated in the lemma. Next,~\ref{it:2140b} allows us to assume, without loss of generality, that 
	 
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:v1}
			|V_0| = (k-1)n - (3k-4)s\,.
	\end{equation}
	 
	In the special case 
	 
	\[
		|V_k|=|V_{2k-1}|=(k-1)n - (3k-4)s
	\]
	 
	we have 
	 
	\[
		n=|V_0|+\ldots +|V_{3k-2}|
		\overset{\eqref{eq:1847}}{\le}
		3\bigl((k-1)n - (3k-4)s\bigr)+(3k-4)(3s-n)=n\,,
	\]
	 
	which yields $|V_i|=3s-n$ for every $i\ne 0, k, 2k-1$, meaning that 
	$a=(k-1)n - (3k-4)s$ exemplifies $H\in \mathscr{G}^n_k(s)$. By symmetry we may 
	therefore suppose $|V_{2k-1}|>(k-1)n - (3k-4)s$ from now on, which  
	in view of Corollary~\ref{blowupedges}\ref{it:2140c} entails
	 
	\[
		s=|N(V_{2k-1})|=|V_0|+\ldots+|V_{k-1}|
		\overset{\eqref{eq:1847}}{\le}
		\bigl((k-1)n - (3k-4)s\bigr)+(k-1)(3s-n)=s\,,
	\]
	 
	i.e., 
	 
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:1903}
		|V_1|=\ldots=|V_{k-1}|=3s-n\,.
	\end{equation}
	 
	Because of $|V_1|+\ldots+|V_k|=|N(V_{2k})|\le s$ and~\eqref{eq:1847} this yields 
	 
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:1911}
		|V_k|=(k-1)n - (3k-4)s\,,
	\end{equation}
	 
	which together with~\eqref{eq:v1} establishes the first bullet in 
	Definition~\ref{def:exan}.
	
	Next we observe that, since by~\eqref{eq:v1} the lower bound on $|V_0|$ provided by 
	Fact~\ref{Vi} holds with equality, an easy inspection of the proof of Fact~\ref{Vi}
	discloses 
	 
		\[
			|V_{k+1}|=\ldots=|V_{2k-2}|=3s-n
		\]
	   
	and for the same reason~\eqref{eq:1911} leads to $|V_{2k+1}|=\ldots=|V_{3k-2}|=3s-n$.
	Combined with~\eqref{eq:1903} these equations confirm the third bullet in
	Definition~\ref{def:exan} and, finally, the second bullet follows easily in the 
	light of $v(H)=n$ and~\eqref{eq:1847}.

label: def:exvega
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:exvega}
	Given natural numbers $k\ge 10$ and $n\ge s\ge 1$ the family $\mathscr{H}^n_k(s)$ is the smallest
	collection of blow-ups of Vega graphs with the following properties. 	
	\begin{enumerate}[label=\upshape({\itshape \alph*\,})]
		\item\label{it:1211a} If  $s = kn/(3k-1)$, then $G^{\mu\nu}_i(3s-n)\in \mathscr{H}^n_k(s)$
			whenever $k=9i-(6+\mu+\nu)$.
		\item\label{it:1211b} If $kn/(3k-1) < s \le (k-1)n/(3k-4)$, then 
			$\Upsilon^{0\nu}_i\bigl((3s-n)\omega_{\mu\nu}-\lambda f\bigr)\in \mathscr{H}^n_k(s)$ whenever $k=9i-(6+\nu)$.
		\item\label{it:1211c} If $kn/(3k-1) < s \le (k-1)n/(3k-4)$, then 
			$\Upsilon^{\mu0}_i\bigl((3s-n)\omega_{\mu\nu}-\lambda g\bigr)\in \mathscr{H}^n_k(s)$ whenever $k=9i-(6+\mu)$.
	\end{enumerate}

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{l:vegaextremal}
	Given integers $i\ge 2$, $\mu, \nu \in \{0,1\}$, and $n\ge s\ge 1$, let $H$ be a blow-up 
	of ${\Upsilon}_{i}^{\mu\nu}$ on $n$ vertices. If

		\alpha(H)\le s
		\quad \text{ and } \quad 
		e(H)=g_k(n,s)
	\]
	 
	hold for $k=9i-(6+\mu+\nu)$, then $H$ is isomorphic to a graph in the 
	family~$\mathscr{H}^n_{k}(s)$.

label: Vegaup
title: Fact
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The upper bound on $|X| +|Y|$ follows from  
	 
	\begin{multline*}
		|X| +|Y| + 2n
		 = 
		|N(A)| + |N(V)| + |N(C)| + |N(U)| + |N(B)|+|N(W)| 
		\overset{\eqref{eq:nh}}{\le}6s\,.
	\end{multline*}
	 
	Similarly,  
	 
	\begin{multline*}
		|V_0| + |V_{2i-1}| + 2n
		 = 
		|N(A)| + |N(B)| + |N(U)| + |N(V)| + |N(V_{i-1})|+|N(V_i)| 
		\overset{\eqref{eq:nh}}{\le}
		6s
	\end{multline*}
	  
	yields the desired upper bound on $|V_0| + |V_{2i-1}|$. It remains to prove 
	$|Z|\le \omega_{\mu\nu}(z)(3s-n)$ for every $z\in V(\Upsilon_i)\smallsetminus\{v_0, v_{2i-1}, x, y\}$.
	Following the same strategy we have just used, this task reduces to exhibiting 
	a list of $3\omega_{\mu\nu}(z)$ vertices of $\Upsilon_i$ whose neighbourhoods cover the 
	entire vertex set $\omega_{\mu\nu}(z)$ many times and the set $Z$ itself even once more.
	As there are several cases and plenty of vertices to consider, it seems useful
	to devise the following notation. For a set $Q\subseteq V(\Upsilon_i)$ we denote
	its characteristic function by ${\mathds 1}(Q)$, so
	 
	\[
		{\mathds 1}(Q)(q)=
			\begin{cases}
				1 & \text{ if $q\in Q$} \cr
				0 & \text{ otherwise} \cr
			\end{cases}
	\]
	 
	for all $q\in V(\Upsilon_i)$.
	If $Q=\{q_1, \ldots, q_r\}$ comes with 
	an explicit enumeration of its members, it will be convenient to omit a pair of curly
	braces, thus writing ${\mathds 1}(q_1, \ldots, q_r)$ for this function. For instance, 
	the functions $f$ and~$g$ considered earlier can now be represented as 
	 
	\[
		f={\mathds 1}(u, v, w, y)-{\mathds 1}(x)
		\quad \text{ and } \quad 
		g={\mathds 1}(b, v, v_{i-1}, v_{2i-1})-{\mathds 1}(v_0)\,.
	\]
	 
	Instead of ${\mathds 1}\bigl(V(\Upsilon_i)\bigr)$ we shall just write ${\mathds 1}$.
	Next, given a function $h\colon V(\Upsilon_i)\longrightarrow{\mathds Z}$ 
	we let $\Sigma(h)=h(V(\Upsilon_i))=\sum_{t\in V(\Upsilon_i)}h(t)$ 
	be the sum of the values it attains
	and by $\mathscr{N}(h)\colon V(\Upsilon_i)\longrightarrow{\mathds Z}$ we mean the function
	$\sum_{t\in V(\Upsilon_i)}h(t)\,{\mathds 1}\bigl(N(t)\bigr)$. In other words, this function satisfies 
	 
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:1205}
		\mathscr{N}(h)(t)=\sum_{t'\in N(t)} h(t') = h\bigl(N(t)\bigr)
		\quad \text{ for every } t\in V(\Upsilon_i)\,.
	\end{equation}
	 
	So we used earlier that 
	 
	\begin{align}
		\mathscr{N}(f)&={\mathds 1}+{\mathds 1}(y)\,, & \Sigma(f)&=3\,, \notag \\
		\text{and } \quad \mathscr{N}(g)&={\mathds 1}+{\mathds 1}(v_{2i-1})\,, &  \Sigma(g)&=3 \,, \label{eq:1051} 
	\end{align}
	  
	the upper bound on $|X|+|Y|$ relies on the fact that the hexagon $\mathscr{C}_6=\{a,v,c,u,b,w\}$
	has the properties 
	 
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:1043}
		\mathscr{N}\bigl({\mathds 1}(\mathscr{C}_6)\bigr)=2\cdot {\mathds 1}+{\mathds 1}(x, y)\,,
		\quad
		\Sigma\bigl({\mathds 1}(\mathscr{C}_6)\bigr)=|\mathscr{C}_6|=6
	\end{equation}
	 
	and soon we are going to need that the inner Andr\'asfai graph 
	$\Gamma=\{v_0,v_1,\dots, v_{3i-2}\}$ satisfies 
	 
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:1203}
		\mathscr{N}\bigl({\mathds 1}(\Gamma)\bigr)=i\cdot {\mathds 1}(\Gamma)+(i-1)\cdot {\mathds 1}(\mathscr{C}_6)+{\mathds 1}(a, b, u, v)\,,
		\qquad
		\Sigma\bigl({\mathds 1}(\Gamma)\bigr)=|\Gamma|=3i-1\,.
	\end{equation}
	 

	Now it suffices to exhibit for every vertex $z\in V(\Upsilon_i)\smallsetminus\{v_0, v_{2i-1}, x, y\}$
	a function 
	 
	\[
		h^z\colon V(\Upsilon_i)\longrightarrow {\mathds Z}_{\ge 0}
	\]
	 
	such that 
	\begin{enumerate}[label=\upshape({\itshape \alph*\,})]
		\item\label{it:0111a} $\mathscr{N}(h^z)$ agrees on $V(\Upsilon^{\mu\nu}_i)$
			with $\omega_{\mu\nu}(z)\cdot {\mathds 1}+{\mathds 1}(z)$ 
		\item\label{it:0111b} and $\Sigma(h^z)=3\omega_{\mu\nu}(z)$.
	\end{enumerate}
	Indeed, once we have such a function $h^z$ at our disposal, we can imitate the 
	above reasoning and argue that 
	 
	\begin{align*}
		\omega_{\mu\nu}(z)n+|Z|
		&\overset{\text{\ref{it:0111a}}}{=}
		\sum_{t\in V(\Upsilon_i)}\mathscr{N}(h^z)(t) |T|
		\overset{\eqref{eq:1205}}{=} 
		\sum_{t\in V(\Upsilon_i)} \sum_{t'\in N(t)} h^z(t') \,|T| \\
		&= 
		\sum_{t'\in V(\Upsilon_i)} h^z(t')\, |N(T')|
		\overset{\eqref{eq:nh}}{\le}  
		\Sigma(h^z) s
		\overset{\text{\ref{it:0111b}}}{=}
		3\omega_{\mu\nu}(z) s\,,
	\end{align*}
	 
	which proves the desired inequality $|Z|\le \omega_{\mu\nu}(z)(3s-n)$.
	
	Starting with the vertices in $\Gamma$ we observe that for every 
	$k\in {\mathds Z}_{3i-1}\smallsetminus\{0, 2i-1\}$ we have 
	 
	\[
		\mathscr{N}\bigl({\mathds 1}(v_{k-i}, v_k, v_{k+i})\bigr)={\mathds 1}(\mathscr{C}_6)+{\mathds 1}(\Gamma)+{\mathds 1}(v_k)\,.
	\]
	 
	By adding~\eqref{eq:1043} we infer 
	 
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:1212}
		\mathscr{N}\bigl({\mathds 1}(\mathscr{C}_6)+{\mathds 1}(v_{k-i}, v_k, v_{k+i})\bigr)=3\cdot{\mathds 1}+{\mathds 1}(v_k)\,,
	\end{equation}
	 
	which shows that for $k\ne 0, i-1, 2i-1$ the function 
	$h^{v_k}={\mathds 1}(\mathscr{C}_6)+{\mathds 1}(v_{k-i}, v_k, v_{k+i})$ has the required properties.
	Moreover, for $k=i-1$ we deduce from~\eqref{eq:1212} with the help 
	of~\eqref{eq:1051} that 
	 
	\[
		\mathscr{N}\bigl({\mathds 1}(\mathscr{C}_6)+{\mathds 1}(v_{i-1}, v_{2i-1}, v_{3i-2})-\nu g\bigr)
		=
		(3-\nu){\mathds 1}+{\mathds 1}(v_{i-1})-\nu{\mathds 1}(v_{2i-1})\,,
	\]
	 
	meaning that we can take $h^{v_{i-1}}={\mathds 1}(\mathscr{C}_6)+{\mathds 1}(v_{i-1}, v_{2i-1}, v_{3i-2})
	-\nu g$. It remains to deal with the vertices on the hexagon. Starting with $a$, 
	we observe 
	 
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:1246}
		\mathscr{N}\bigl({\mathds 1}(a, x)-{\mathds 1}(v_{2i-1})\bigr)={\mathds 1}(a, c, w, x, y)\,,
	\end{equation}
	 
	which in view of~\eqref{eq:1043} and~\eqref{eq:1203} entails that the function
	 
	\[
		h^a=(i-1){\mathds 1}(\mathscr{C}_6) +{\mathds 1}(\Gamma)+{\mathds 1}(a, x)-{\mathds 1}(v_{2i-1})
	\]
	  
	satisfies 
	 
	\begin{multline*}
		\mathscr{N}(h^a)
		=[(2i-2)\cdot {\mathds 1}+(i-1)\cdot {\mathds 1}(x, y)] 
		+[i\cdot{\mathds 1}(\Gamma)+(i-1)\cdot{\mathds 1}(\mathscr{C}_6) +{\mathds 1}(a, b, u, v)] \\
		+ {\mathds 1}(a, c, w, x, y) =(3i-2)\cdot{\mathds 1}+{\mathds 1}(a)\,.
	\end{multline*}
	 
	Together with $\Sigma(h^a)=6(i-1)+(3i-1)+2-1=3(3i-2)$ this proves that $h^a$ 
	has all required properties. By symmetry, for 
	$\widetilde{h}^b=(i-1)\cdot{\mathds 1}(\mathscr{C}_6) +{\mathds 1}(\Gamma)+{\mathds 1}(b, x)-{\mathds 1}(v_{0})$
	we obtain $\mathscr{N}(\widetilde{h}^b)=(3i-2){\mathds 1}+{\mathds 1}(b)$ and 
	$\Sigma(\widetilde{h}^b)=3(3i-2)$,
	so by~\eqref{eq:1051} we may set $h^b=\widetilde{h}^b-\nu g$.
	Next, 
	 
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:1415}
		\mathscr{N}\bigl({\mathds 1}(x)-{\mathds 1}(v_0, v_{2i-1}, w)\bigr)
		=
		{\mathds 1}(c)-{\mathds 1}(a, b, u, v)-{\mathds 1}(\Gamma)
	\end{equation}
	   
	reveals that the function 
	$h^c=(i-1)\cdot{\mathds 1}(\mathscr{C}_6)+{\mathds 1}(\Gamma)+{\mathds 1}(x)-{\mathds 1}(v_0, v_{2i-1}, w)$
	has the property 
	 
	\begin{multline*}
		\mathscr{N}(h^c)=[(2i-2)\cdot{\mathds 1}+(i-1)\cdot{\mathds 1}(x, y)]
			+[i\cdot{\mathds 1}(\Gamma)+(i-1)\cdot{\mathds 1}(\mathscr{C}_6)+{\mathds 1}(a, b, u, v)] \\
			+[{\mathds 1}(c)-{\mathds 1}(a, b, u, v)-{\mathds 1}(\Gamma)]  = (3i-3){\mathds 1}+{\mathds 1}(c)
	\end{multline*}
	 
	and because of $\Sigma(h^c)=6(i-1)+(3i-1)+1-3=3(3i-3)$ this establishes 
	the desired bound $|C|\le (3i-3)(3s-n)$. 
	Utilising that similar to~\eqref{eq:1246},~\eqref{eq:1415} we 
	have 
	 
	\begin{align*}
		\mathscr{N}\bigl({\mathds 1}(u, y)-{\mathds 1}(v_{2i-1})\bigr) &={\mathds 1}(c, u, w, x, y) \\
		\mathscr{N}\bigl({\mathds 1}(v, y)-{\mathds 1}(v_{0})\bigr) &= {\mathds 1}(c, v, w, x, y) \\
		\text{ and } \quad \mathscr{N}\bigl({\mathds 1}(y)-{\mathds 1}(c, v_0, v_{2i-1})\bigr)
			&={\mathds 1}(w)-{\mathds 1}(a, b, u, v)-{\mathds 1}(\Gamma)
	\end{align*}
	 
	one confirms easily that the functions 
	 
	\begin{align*}
		h^u &=(i-1){\mathds 1}(\mathscr{C}_6)+{\mathds 1}(\Gamma)+{\mathds 1}(u, y)-{\mathds 1}(v_{2i-1})-\mu f \\
		h^v &=(i-1){\mathds 1}(\mathscr{C}_6)+{\mathds 1}(\Gamma) +{\mathds 1}(v, y)-{\mathds 1}(v_0)-\mu f-\nu g \\
		\text{ and } \quad 
		h^w &=(i-1){\mathds 1}(\mathscr{C}_6)+{\mathds 1}(\Gamma)+{\mathds 1}(y)-{\mathds 1}(c, v_0, v_{2i-1})-\mu f
	\end{align*}
	 
	take care of the three remaining vertex classes.

title: Proof
body_md:
Recall that in the proof of Lemma~\ref{l:vegaex} we viewed $H$ as a blow-up of 
	the $k$-regular graph $G_i^{\mu\nu}$. By Corollary~\ref{blowupedges} at least
	one of the particles occurring in this construction has the 
	size $(k-1)n-(3k-4)s = (3s-n) - \lambda$. Let $z\in V({\Upsilon}_{i}^{\mu\nu})$ be a vertex one of 
	whose~$\omega_{\mu\nu}(z)$ particles has this size. Now~\eqref{eq:226} needs to hold with 
	equality and we have $\lceil \lambda/\omega_{\mu\nu}(z)\rceil=\lambda$. For this reason 
	at least one of the equations $\omega_{\mu\nu}(z)=1$ or $\lambda=1$ is true.  
	In the former case, $z\in \{x, y, v_0, v_{2i-1}\}$ is immediate and we are done. 
	
	Now suppose for the sake of contradiction that $\lambda=1$ 
	and that $|Z|\ne 3s-n-\lambda$ holds for every $z\in V({\Upsilon}_{i}^{\mu\nu})\cap\{x, y, v_0, v_{2i-1}\}$ 
	with $\omega_{\mu\nu}(z)=1$. Together with the Facts~\ref{Vegaup} and~\ref{Vegadown} this 
	yields $|Z|\le \omega_{\mu\nu}(z)(3s-n)$ for all vertices $z\in V({\Upsilon}_{i}^{\mu\nu})$. 
	
	Concerning the set $M=\{z\in V({\Upsilon}_{i}^{\mu\nu})\colon |Z| < \omega_{\mu\nu}(z)(3s-n)\}$ of vertices for which 
	this estimate fails to be sharp we can deduce from 
	 
	\[
		 n=\sum_{z\in V({\Upsilon}_{i}^{\mu\nu})} |Z| \le \omega_{\mu\nu}\bigl(V({\Upsilon}_{i}^{\mu\nu})\bigr)(3s-n) -|M|
	\]
	 
	and~\eqref{eq:1709} that $|M|\le 3$. Owing to $\chi({\Upsilon}_{i}^{\mu\nu})=4$ this shows that the neighbourhoods
	of the vertices in $M$ cannot cover the entire vertex sets of ${\Upsilon}_{i}^{\mu\nu}$ or, in other words, that 
	there is a vertex $z_\star\in V({\Upsilon}_{i}^{\mu\nu})$ whose neighbourhood is disjoint to $M$.	
	But now 
	 
	\[
		s
		\ge 
		|N(Z_\star)| 
		= 
		\sum_{z\in N(z_\star)}|Z|
		= 
		\sum_{z\in N(z_\star)}\omega_{\mu\nu}(z)(3s-n)
		=
		k(3s-n)
	\]
	 
	contradicts~\eqref{eq:vs}. This completes the proof of Claim~\ref{clm:1315}.

\label{f:s}
	If $n\ge s \ge 1$ and $k\ge 2$ are such that 
	${s\notin \bigl(\frac{k}{3k-1}n, \frac{k-1}{3k-4}n\bigr)}$, then 
	 
	\[
	\mathrm{ex}(n,s)\le g_k(n, s)

title: Proof
body_md:
Observe that adding any edges to $H$ can neither increase its independence number 
	nor decrease its minimum degree. Thus, we may and shall assume that~$H$ is a maximal
	triangle-free graph.
	
	Due to Fact~\ref{f:s}, it suffices to consider the case
	 
	\[
		\Delta(H) \le \alpha(H) \le s < \frac{k-1}{3k-4}n\,.
	\]
	 
	Since $\delta(H) > (k+1)n/(3k+2) > n/3$, Theorem~\ref{th:dense} tells us 
	that $H$ is a proper blow-up of some graph $J$, which is either
	an Andr\'asfai graph $\Gamma_{\ell}$, or a Vega graph ${\Upsilon}_{i}^{\mu\nu}$. 
	In the latter case we set $\ell=9i-(6+\mu+\nu)$. Now in both cases $J$ has 
	a proper $\ell$-regular blow-up on $3\ell-1$ vertices and Lemma \ref{l:kregular} 
	yields $k = \ell$. 
	If $J=\Gamma_k$ is an Andr\'asfai graph the assertion follows from Lemma~\ref{ag0} 
	and if $J$ is a Vega graph we use Lemma~\ref{l:vegaex} instead.

name: Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:mindeg}

label: eq:1704
title: Proof
body_md:
Define   
	 
	\[
		\zeta=\frac{1}{8k^2}
		\quad\text{ and } \quad
		\gamma=\frac{1}{600k^6}\,.
	\]
	   
	Consider a triangle-free graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with $\alpha(G)\le s$ 
	and $e(G)=\mathrm{ex}(n,s)$, where 
	 
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:1704}
		\frac{k}{3k-1}n \le  s \le \left(\frac{k}{3k-1}+\gamma\right)n\,.
	\end{equation}
	 
	
	Since $\gamma$ is sufficiently small, we have $s<(k-1)n/(3k-4)$ and 
	Fact~\ref{f:s} implies $e(G)\le g_\ell(n, s)$ for every $\ell\ne k$. 
	On the other hand, Lemma~\ref{lem:2130} yields
	 
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:0007}
		e(G)=\mathrm{ex}(n,s)\ge g_k(n,s)
	\end{equation}
	and it remains to prove that this holds with equality. It will be convenient to 
	rewrite~\eqref{eq:0007} as
	 
	\[
		e(G)
		\ge 
		g_k(n,s)
		=
		\tfrac12\bigl[ns-\bigl((k-1)n -(3k-4)s\bigr)\bigl((3k-1)s - kn\bigr)\bigr]\,.
	\]
	 
	Since
	 
	\[
		0 \le (3k-1)s-kn < 3k\gamma n
	\]
	 
	and 
	 
	\[
		(k-1)n-(3k-4)s \le \frac{(3k-1)(k-1)}k s-(3k-4)s =\frac sk\,,
	\]
	 
	we have 
	 
	\[
		\bigl((k-1)n-(3k-4)s\bigr) \bigl((3k-1)s-kn\bigr)<3\gamma ns\,,
	\]
	 
	and thus
	 
	\[
	ns-2e(G) < 3\gamma ns\,.
	\]
	 
	
	Therefore, the set 
	   
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:Adef}
		A=\left\{v\in V(G)\colon d(v) < \left(1-\zeta\right)s\right\}
	\end{equation}
	 
	satisfies 
	 
	\[
	\zeta s|A|\le \sum_{v\in V}\left(s-d(v)\right)=ns-2e(G) < 3\gamma ns
	\]
	 
	and, consequently, 
	 
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:0027}
	|A| < \frac{3\gamma n}\zeta =\frac n{25k^4}\,.
	\end{equation}
	 
	
	Now our argument will proceed as follows. We shall verify 	
	that the graph $G'=G-A$ satisfies the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:mindeg} 
	and, hence, $e(G')$ is bounded from above by $g_k(n-|A|,s)$. Then, using the 
	fact that all vertices in $A$ are of small degree, we derive an upper bound 
	of $g_k(n,s)$ on the number of edges in $G$.
	
	For the minimum degree of $G'$ we obtain 
	 
	\begin{align*}
		\delta(G') &\ge \left(1-\zeta\right)s-|A| 
		> \frac{k}{3k-1}n-\frac{n/2}{8k^2}-\frac{n}{25k^4}\\	
		&>\left(\frac{k+1}{3k+2}+\frac{1}{12k^2}-\frac 1{16k^2}-\frac 1{100k^2}\right)n \\
		&> \frac{k+1}{3k+2}n \ge \frac{k+1}{3k+2} |V(G')|\,.                       
	\end{align*}
	 
	As the graph $G'$ is triangle-free and satisfies $\alpha(G')\le s$, this shows that 
	Theorem~\ref{thm:mindeg} applies to~$G'$ and we are led to 
	 
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:0028}
		e(G')\le g_k(n-|A|,s)
		=
		g_k(n, s)-|A|\left(k(k-1)n-\tfrac 12k(k-1)|A|-k(3k-4)s\right)\,.
	\end{equation}
	 
	Now our choice of $\zeta$ and $\gamma$ yields 
	 
	\begin{align*}
		\bigl((k-1)(3k-1)-\zeta\bigr)s
		&\le 
		\left((k-1)(3k-1)-\frac 1{8k^2}\right)\left(\frac k{3k-1}+\frac 1{600k^6}\right)n \\
		&<
		\left(k(k-1) +\frac 1{200k^4}-\frac 1{8k(3k-1)}\right)n \\
		&<
		\left(k(k-1) +\frac 1{50k^2}-\frac 1{25k^2}\right)n
		<k(k-1)\left(1-\frac 1{50k^4}\right)n \\
		&
		\overset{\eqref{eq:0027}}{<}
		k(k-1)(n-\tfrac 12 |A|)\,,
	\end{align*}
	 
	and for this reason~\eqref{eq:0028} can be continued to 
	 
	\begin{align*}
		e(G')&\le g_k(n, s)-\bigl((k-1)(3k-1)-\zeta-k(3k-4)\bigr)|A|s \\ 
		&= g_k(n,s) - (1-\zeta)|A|s\,.
	\end{align*}
	 
	Every vertex in $A$ has degree at most $(1-\zeta)s$ in $G$, so we arrive at
	 
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:0103}
		e(G)\le e(G')+(1-\zeta)|A|s\le  g_k(n, s)\,,
	\end{equation}
	 
	which together with~\eqref{eq:0007} concludes the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.

name: Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}

title: Corollary
body_md:
Suppose that $k\ge 2$ and that $G$ denotes a triangle-free graph on $n$ 
	vertices with $\alpha(G)\le s$ for some integer $s$ satisfying
	 
	\[
		\frac{k}{3k-1}n \le  s \le \left(\frac{k}{3k-1}+\frac 1{600k^6}\right)n\,.
	\]
	  
	If $e(G)=\mathrm{ex}(n, s)$, then $G$ is isomorphic to a graph in $\mathscr{G}^n_k(s)\cup\mathscr{H}^n_k(s)$.
